data.content_ref: inline:exp-hist:{"target": "1252bd6fa24e5e25116ce4579b7cfc5218a41f71421dbcdeef07817141cb1d26", "seq": 1, "objection": "The target's defense collapses because it relies on 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) as the objective ground for preferring better-corroborated theories, yet Popper's own formal definition of verisimilitude was proven logically incoherent by Tichý and Miller in 1974. They demonstrated that under Popper's own criteria, no false theory can be said to be closer to the truth than another; consequently, the 'objective logic of situation' the target cites cannot exist as formulated. Without a coherent measure of verisimilitude, the preference for the better-corroborated theory reverts to an unjustified assumption that past survival indicates greater closeness to truth, which is precisely the inductive leap the target claims to avoid.", "outcome": "raised and not answered; the target's status did not move"}
